Author: @mlggamer5296
Content: Copper golems are actually very easy to utilize all you have to do is make sure you put things inside your chest that you want organized then you need to put the stuff that you need to organize inside the copper chests and then they'll organized by looking through your chest to find the matching remainder of them. They pick up groups of I think it was 16 or 32 blocks or items. I will give an example let's say you're organizing dirt. Maybe you have a chest full of regular dirt mycelium in another chest grass in another etc. if you don't have a full stack of each in each of the chests that's going to help and then you just place all your dirt and everything that you want organized into the copper chest. Copper golem goes in, takes 16 of them and then he looks through the chests to find which one is corresponding to the dirt they just picked up. You really don't need to be mumbo jumbo for that. Just put samples of what you want organized into the chests and then everything else in the copper chests

Content:
In terms of nautilus armour, you can find 4 types naturally spawning in shipwrecks and ocean ruin chests: Copper, gold, iron and diamond, each one rarer and more protective than the last. (Be warned that diamond is around a 1% chance per loot chest, so it might take a fair few to get it). You can upgrade diamond nautilus armour to netherite the same way you upgrade player armour, with a netherite upgrade template and a netherite ingot, which makes it even better at protecting. 

I'd suggest going for at least iron or diamond at the moment considering how many trident Drowned hang out under the base, but if you really want to splash out, then netherite would be the best investment

Author: @djwitheredbonnie4560
Content:
Dan! I'm one of the Minecraft P,layers who dedicates their time on fishing on both Bedrock and Java. A fishing rod with Luck of the Sea III, Lure III, Unbreaking III and Mending is the max you can get on a fishing rod, and the best fishing rod you can get as well.

You are now able to get really good things from just fishing ALONE, but there's a catch. If it's raining or if it's a thunderstorm, your chances of catching fish is far greater during those times than if you fish when then the weather is clear. If you ever aim to sit there and fish for enchanted books, don't do it while it's raining. Fishing is also not a bad sourse of XP either, since you get it while fishing and you can get XP from any Enchanted Bows and/or Fishing Rods you might get (via a Grindstone). It's oddly impressive you can level up from fishing alone if you can't find any either methods at the moment.

Also, I'm aware that fishing farms exist, but this is more or less me giving out some tips regardless if he uses a automatic fishing contraption or not.

Also also, fishing rod name recommendation: *Lure Of The Unbreakable Mend*
